name: East River band 1: Pearl St to Water St (State St to Dover St)
note: Inner edge Pearl St = the shoreline before fill (it approximates the 1609 high-water line; where the mapped 1609 shore differs, that wins). Water lots between high and low water were sold under the Dongan Charter of 1686 (first grant on the Fraunces Tavern block 19 Nov 1686); the waterfront had moved to Water St by 1730. Start and end documented; progress inside the span is not.

name: East River band 2: Water St to Front St (Whitehall St to Dover St)
note: Water lots to 400 ft beyond low water came with the Montgomerie Charter (1731); waterfront at Front St "in 1780"; the slips between Water and Front St at Burling/Beekman Slip were filled by 1788 (Schermerhorn Row). Front St is demapped south-west of Old Slip: there the outer line is Water St offset by the Water-Front spacing at Old Slip (estimated line).

name: East River band 3: Front St to South St and the bulkhead (Whitehall St to Dover St)
note: The city began to grade South St in 1798; South St "created by 1810"; at Schermerhorn Row the shore did not reach South St until the 1810s. Outer edge = today's bulkhead (Overture water, at most 80 m beyond the South St centre line); the few metres outboard of old South St belong to the Department of Docks bulkhead wall of 1871 onward and are not split off.

name: Two Bridges: Cherry St to Water St (Dover St to Jackson St)
note: The pre-fill shore "generally ran along Pearl and Cherry streets"; fill here began at the end of the 18th century (ESCR Phase 1A). Dates are an estimated bracket, not a documented progression; Cherry St is demapped between Dover and Catherine St (straight line used).

name: Two Bridges: Water St to South St and the bulkhead (Dover St to Jackson St)
note: South St created by 1810 at its lower end; between Montgomery and Rivington St the strip along the river was filled "at various times between the 1810s and about 1850" (ESCR Phase 1A). Estimated bracket.

name: Lower East Side waterfront: Columbia St / Avenue D to the old bulkhead (FDR Drive), Corlears Hook to E 14th St
note: Whole strip was under the East River and was filled "at various times between the 1810s and about 1850"; the corner at Corlears St / Water St (East River Park amphitheatre) only in the 1870s-80s (not split off). Inner line Jackson St - Columbia St - Avenue D only brackets the area. North of Rivington St the same bracket is assumed (estimated).

name: East River Park fill outboard of the old bulkhead (Jackson St to E 14th St)
note: Between the historic bulkhead line and the present bulkhead "landfilled in the 20th century in conjunction with the creation of East River Park"; present bulkhead 1930s; park opened 27 July 1939. Start year estimated. Inner edge = FDR Drive centre line standing for the old bulkhead.

name: Stuyvesant salt meadows (1st Avenue to Avenue D, Houston St to E 14th St)
note: "Most of present-day Alphabet City was a salt marsh" (Tompkins Square Park stands on it). The debate about grading and draining its streets "went round and round for over a decade, even as filling proceeded" (committee of 1823); in 1832 "no amount of fill seemed to stem periodic flooding". Ring only brackets the marsh; both years estimated from those statements.

name: Stuyvesant Cove / Gas House district: 1st Avenue to the old bulkhead, E 14th to E 23rd St
note: Cove of the East River north of the meadows, later the Gas House district. Estimated bracket (no source found with dates for these blocks; the blocks just north were filled from the late 1830s through the second half of the 19th century).

name: Bellevue waterfront: 1st Avenue to the old bulkhead, E 23rd to E 34th St
note: E 23rd and E 25th St began as piers in the late 1830s, E 24th in the 1870s; the blocks were filled in stages through the second half of the 19th century, the block E 24th-25th (Asser Levy) only in the 1890s. Documented bracket.

name: East River Drive fill outboard of the old bulkhead, E 14th to E 23rd St
note: Land east of the drive (Stuyvesant Cove Park, Con Edison pier side). The drive opened from 12th to 18th St in 1939 and was continuous from Montgomery to 30th St in May 1940; the area E 23rd-25th was "landfilled between the 1830s and the 1940s". Start year estimated.

name: Bristol Basin: East River Drive fill, E 23rd to E 34th St
note: This section of the drive was built on rubble from bombed Bristol, brought back as ballast by ships returning from England; the 23rd-34th St section was completed in October 1941 (plaque dedicated 29 June 1942). Start year estimated. Inner edge 20 m west of the drive centre line.

name: Hudson band 1: Greenwich St to Washington St (Battery Place to Chambers St)
note: High-water mark of the 1873 Department of Docks map lay about Greenwich St between the Battery and Chambers St, low water east of Washington St (it approximates the 1609 line; where the mapped 1609 shore differs, that wins). A ship of the 1770s-80s found at the World Trade Center was in the fill by the 1790s. Start year estimated (water lots after the Montgomerie Charter); end = the 1797 Taylor-Roberts plan.

name: Hudson band 1 north: Greenwich St to Washington St (Chambers St to Gansevoort St)
note: North of Chambers St fast land reached west of Greenwich St in places (Vesey to North Moore St) and the bank was at Washington St at Gansevoort St, so only part of this band is made land: intersect with the 1609 shore. Dates estimated; the 1797 and 1808 plans show the shore near Washington St at North Moore St.

name: Hudson band 2: Washington St to West St (Battery Place to Gansevoort St)
note: Landfilling "intensified at the turn of the 19th century"; water lots at North Moore / Harrison / Jay St granted 1805-07 and not yet filled on the 1808 plan; the bed of West St "largely filled" by the 1836 Colton map. Outer edge = west side of the 70 ft West St (northbound carriageway centre line + 10.7 m). Washington St is closed between Barclay and Hubert St (straight line used).

name: Hudson band 3: West St to the Department of Docks bulkhead (Battery Place to Gansevoort St)
note: Bulkhead line of 1871, 250 ft west of the line of West St; the masonry bulkhead wall and the marginal street behind it were built 1871-1935 over the whole Hudson front, here c.1890s-1903. Measured on the data: today's wall is 61-63 m west of the northbound carriageway from Tribeca to Gansevoort St.

name: Battery Park City
note: Fill between the 1871 bulkhead and the pierhead line: the southern part from the World Trade Center excavation (from 1966-68), the rest with dredged sand and other spoil; "landfill construction was finished" July 1976. Start year estimated from the WTC excavation; the south-to-north order is not split.

name: The Battery before 1855 (about 10 acres next to State St and Whitehall St)
note: State St approximates the original waterline. Earth platforms were built off the tip in 1683 and 1735, the rubble of Fort George was added after 1788, and by the 1820s the park was about 10 acres. The ring is the 10 acres of today's Battery nearest State St / Whitehall St (estimated outline, real area).

name: Battery extension that joined Castle Garden's island
note: Castle Clinton (West Battery, 1808-11) stood on an artificial island 200 ft offshore. The park was enlarged with spoil from street widening "starting from 1855", and about 1869 the island was joined to Manhattan; by 1870 the enlarged park was complete enough to need "improvement" (end year estimated). Outer edge = today's sea wall; inner edge is the estimated limit of the earlier Battery.

name: Thirteenth Avenue fill (W 11th St to W 22nd St), including the Gansevoort peninsula
note: Thirteenth Avenue "was built in 1837 on landfill" west of West St / 11th Avenue, from 11th St to about 29th St. The ring is the made land that is water again today plus the surviving Gansevoort peninsula: east edge today's bulkhead, west edge the line of the peninsula's outer face carried north and south. End year estimated (the fill went on for some decades).

name: Thirteenth Avenue fill removed for the Gansevoort piers (W 11th St to Gansevoort St)
note: The city removed the landfill on which Thirteenth Avenue ran south of 22nd St so that longer piers could be built without passing the federal pierhead line; the Chelsea Piers opened in 1910. Start year estimated. Same outline as the matching part of mn_hr_13th_avenue_fill; the Gansevoort peninsula (West Washington Market) stayed.

name: Thirteenth Avenue fill removed for the Chelsea Piers (Gansevoort peninsula to W 22nd St)
note: The city removed the landfill on which Thirteenth Avenue ran south of 22nd St so that longer piers could be built without passing the federal pierhead line; the Chelsea Piers opened in 1910. Start year estimated. Same outline as the matching part of mn_hr_13th_avenue_fill; the Gansevoort peninsula (West Washington Market) stayed.

name: Chelsea waterfront: Washington St / 10th Avenue to the bulkhead, Gansevoort St to W 23rd St
note: The bank was at Washington St at Gansevoort St; Thirteenth Avenue beyond was filled from 1837. Inner line only brackets the area; dates estimated (no source found that dates the fill between 10th and 11th Avenues).

name: Hudson shore W 23rd St to W 59th St: 10th Avenue to the bulkhead
note: Includes the Thirteenth Avenue fill of 1837 onward north of 22nd St and the bay at the foot of 42nd St (Great Kill). Estimated bracket; bulkhead wall 1871-1935.

name: Hudson shore W 59th St to W 72nd St (former 60th Street rail yard, Riverside South)
note: The 57 acres "just south of Riverside Park that had been the Penn Central freight rail yard". Estimated bracket; no source found that dates the fill.

name: Riverside Park fill west of Riverside Drive, W 72nd St to W 122nd St
note: West Side Improvement: the parkway "was to be built on newly filled land along the shore", approved June 1935, completed 1937, adding 132 acres to the park and covering the railroad. City-owned underwater land had already been filled in 1911-12 with rock from the Catskill Aqueduct. The ring runs from Riverside Drive; only the part west of the 1609 shore is made land.

name: Hudson shore W 122nd St to W 155th St (Manhattanville, Riverbank)
note: Railroad along the water's edge, the Manhattanville waterfront, then the parkway fill of the 1930s. Estimated bracket; no source found with dates.

name: Hudson shore W 155th St to Dyckman St (Fort Washington Park)
note: Parkway and park fill outside the railroad. Estimated bracket, taken from the years of the Riverside Park parkway fill (approved 1935, completed 1937); no source found for this reach.

name: Kips Bay: 1st Avenue to the old bulkhead, E 34th to E 42nd St
note: Kips Bay was an inlet of the East River from about 32nd to 37th St. No source found for when it was filled; estimated bracket.

name: Turtle Bay: 2nd Avenue to the old bulkhead, E 42nd to E 49th St
note: Cove of the East River between 45th and 48th St. "By 1868 the bay had been entirely filled in"; start year estimated.

name: East River Drive, E 34th to E 49th St: made land and deck outboard of the old shore
note: Last part of the original drive, opened May 1942. Partly fill, partly deck over the river; start year estimated.

name: East River Drive, E 49th to E 96th St: made land and deck outboard of the old shore
note: Opened June 1940. Much of this shore is rock bluff with the drive on a shelf or in tunnels (Sutton Place, Carl Schurz Park), so only the part outside the 1609 shore is made land. Start year estimated.

name: East River Drive, E 96th to E 125th St: fill outboard of the old bulkhead
note: Section from 125th St south to 92nd St "completed in 1936". Start year estimated.

name: Harlem Creek marsh and the East Harlem flats: 5th Avenue to the East River, E 96th to E 125th St
note: Harlem Creek ran into Harlem Marsh, a partly tidal wetland between about 106th and 110th St draining to the East River, later "buried beneath the city's expanding street grid". Dates estimated (1870s-80s, when the grid was built out here); the ring only brackets the marsh and the shore flats.

name: Harlem River flats: 5th / 8th Avenue to the river, 125th to 155th St
note: Low shore and marsh along the Harlem River filled as the grid and the rail yards were built. Estimated bracket; no source found with dates.

name: Harlem River Speedway shelf, W 155th St to Dyckman St
note: The Speedway was built along the riverbank from W 155th St to Dyckman St: construction started 1894, opened July 1898. Ring = from 25 m inland of today's Harlem River Drive to the river.

name: Sherman Creek and the Inwood flats: 10th Avenue to the Harlem River, Dyckman St to W 218th St
note: Tidal inlet (Sherman Creek) and its marsh, now rail yards and housing. Estimated bracket; no source found with dates.

name: Harlem River Ship Canal: the cut between Inwood and Marble Hill
note: Upland of Manhattan cut through: construction started January 1888, the cut at Marble Hill opened 17 June 1895 (a 30 ft "Dyckman canal" had run here since 1817). Ring = today's water lying between Manhattan Island and the Marble Hill tax lots, buffered 15 m; clip to water.

name: Old bed of Spuyten Duyvil Creek round Marble Hill
note: After the canal Marble Hill was an island; "in 1914 the original creekbed was filled in with rock from the excavation of Grand Central Terminal" (another article says joined to the Bronx in 1913). Ring = a 230 m collar round the hull of the Manhattan tax lots north of the canal: it brackets the bed (west, north and east of the hill), it is not its outline.

name: Spuyten Duyvil Creek straightened west of Marble Hill
note: The western end of the creek was straightened: plans final 1935, "the channel was excavated from 1937 to 1938". The flat north end of Inwood Hill Park "is on a peninsula that was formerly connected to the Bronx mainland"; the filling of the old loop behind it is not mapped (no outline on disk, no date found). Ring = today's channel between Inwood Hill Park and the Bronx west of Marble Hill; only the part that was land before 1937 was dug.

name: Collect Pond (Fresh Water Pond) and its margin
note: Fresh-water pond of about 48 acres, up to 60 ft deep. The Common Council ordered it filled in 1803; drained through a canal (1807) and filled with the earth of Bayard's Mount; "the landfill was completed in 1811". Ring of streets brackets the pond (Lafayette - Walker - Baxter - Mulberry - Worth, widened by 100 m); it is not the outline.

name: Lispenard Meadows and the canal along Canal St
note: Salt marsh draining the Collect to the Hudson, drained by the 40 ft ditch that became Canal St (canal dug 1807, "drained by 1813 or 1815", ditch covered 1819). Start year estimated. Ring of streets brackets the meadows.

name: Central Park Reservoir (Upper Reservoir, Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir)
note: Second Croton reservoir in the park, "completed in 1862"; decommissioned 1993, still holds water. Outline = Overture water.

name: Croton receiving reservoir (Yorkville or Lower Reservoir), now the Great Lawn and Turtle Pond
note: Built 1842, filled from 27 June 1842; decommissioned 1903, "began to be drained in January 1930" and filled in for the Great Lawn. Ring = a rectangle of the documented size of the basin (1826 x 836 ft, 14.2 ha), centred on and aligned with today's Great Lawn and Turtle Pond; the walls were not traced, and the size is quoted from memory of the usual figure (estimated).

name: Croton Distributing Reservoir, Fifth Avenue 40th-42nd St (site of the Public Library)
note: Walled basin of 4 acres on Murray Hill, in service from 1842, "torn down in the 1890s" (demolished 1899). Ring = square on the Fifth Avenue front between 40th and 42nd St, 128 m deep (4 acres); the walls were not surveyed.

name: Castle Clinton (West Battery) on its artificial island
note: The West Battery was "erected on a small artificial offshore island" in 1808-1811, 200 ft from the shore and reached by a bridge. Ring = today's footprint of the fort + 12 m. It lies inside mn_battery_1855: the earlier zone wins.

name: Highbridge Reservoir (site of the Highbridge pool)
note: High-service reservoir of about 7 acres beside the water tower: built 1866-1872, unused for some fifteen years by 1934, when it was taken for the Highbridge Play Center pool (opened 1936). Ring = 7-acre circle centred between the recreation centre and the water tower footprints; the real basin was a rounded rectangle.

name: Governors Island: the southern extension
note: The Army Corps of Engineers added 4.787 million cubic yards of fill south of the original island, using material from the first subway line: 103 acres, "mostly finished by 1909-1910 and declared complete by January 1913". Start year estimated from the subway excavation. Ring = the whole island (69.6 ha); the original island is the part north of Division Road / Liggett Hall.

name: Ellis Island, north side (island 1: the original island and the fill round it)
note: The original island was about 3.3 acres; the magazine was ordered torn down 11 April 1890 for the immigration station and the island "was expanded to 14 acres by 1896". Ring = the island north-east of the ferry basin; the natural core inside it is not fill.

name: Ellis Island, south side (islands 2 and 3 and the fill between them)
note: Island 2 (3.33 acres) was finished December 1898, island 3 (4.75 acres) contracted April 1905 and complete 1906 (20.25 acres in all); the basin between islands 2 and 3 was filled in the 1920s; the island reached 27.5 acres in the 1930s (end year 1934 estimated from "between the late 1890s and the 1930s").

name: Little Hell Gate, the channel between Randalls and Wards islands
note: "Infilling took place beginning in the mid-1950s"; the channel "was filled by the early 1960s" (a short inlet remains on the east). Ring = the land within 160 m of both islands as OpenStreetMap divides them; it brackets the old channel.

name: Randalls Island: shore and marsh fill
note: Bracket estimated from the park works of the 1930s to the filling of Little Hell Gate in the early 1960s. Sunken Meadow Island (about 20 acres, to the east) was joined in 1955 and the Hammock "was subsumed through filling operations". Ring = the island as OpenStreetMap divides it, less the Little Hell Gate ring; the natural core is not fill.

name: Wards Island: shore and marsh fill
note: Bracket estimated from the park works of the 1930s to the filling of Little Hell Gate in the early 1960s. Wards Island was about 145 acres, with marsh on its western and northern shores. Ring = the island as OpenStreetMap divides it, less the Little Hell Gate ring; the natural core is not fill.

name: Rikers Island enlargement
note: Sold to the city in 1884; the original island of about 90 acres was enlarged to 415 acres, first with ashes hauled by convict labour, and "landfill continued to be added until 1943". Ring = the whole island; the natural core is not fill.

name: Roosevelt (Blackwell's) Island: shore fill
note: "The island was 107 acres prior to the 18th century but has been expanded to 147 acres"; fill added "since the 19th century". No dated stages found: the bracket is estimated. Ring = the whole island.

name: U Thant (Belmont) Island
note: Artificial islet: spoil from a shaft sunk on Man-o'-War Reef for the Steinway Tunnel built the reef up into an island; the tunnel was completed between 1905 and 1907 (work first started and stopped in 1892).

name: Mill Rock: Great and Little Mill Rock joined
note: "In 1890 the Flood Island remnants were used to fill the space between Great and Little Mill Rocks." Ring = today's islet; the two rocks themselves are natural.

name: Hoffman Island (Upper Quarantine)
note: Artificial island on Orchard Shoal: sand dredged from the harbour was dumped from 1860; the island was "created in 1873".

name: Swinburne Island (Dix Island, Lower Quarantine)
note: Artificial island made of dredged sand from 1860; renamed in 1869 and fitted out as a quarantine station in 1870.

name: Bronx Kill narrowed by fill on the Randalls Island side
note: In 1917 the kill was still to be dredged to 480 ft wide; "much of the Bronx Kill was later filled in to expand the parkland on Randalls Island". No dated source found: estimated bracket. Ring = Randalls Island within 140 m of today's kill.

name: Mount Prospect Reservoir
note: Brooklyn's reservoir on Mount Prospect, built 1856; made redundant by Water Tunnel No. 2 (1936); "demolition of the reservoir began in 1938". Ring = Mount Prospect Park (NYC Parks outline) shrunk by 25 m; the basin itself was not traced.

name: Brooklyn Heights piers, Fulton Ferry and Dumbo: Furman St / Front St to the bulkhead
note: Wharves and warehouse blocks built out from the foot of the Heights and the Fulton Ferry landing. Estimated bracket; no source found with dates. Inner line Furman St and Front St only brackets the area.

name: Wallabout Bay: the Brooklyn Navy Yard and Wallabout Market flats
note: The yard stands on "a mudflat and tidal marsh" of Wallabout Bay; in its wartime enlargement "extensive landfilling operations" removed the market and the Cob Dock and filled the market branch of Wallabout Basin and the Kent Avenue basin. Estimated bracket (founding of the yard to the wartime enlargement); the stages inside it are not mapped.

name: Red Hook and the Columbia Street waterfront: west of Columbia St and Hamilton Avenue
note: Red Hook "was a low-lying area full of tidal mill ponds"; the hook itself was an island. Atlantic Basin was dredged in 1850 and Erie Basin in 1864, with the marsh round them filled for the docks. Estimated bracket; the basins are water and stay water.

name: Gowanus Creek marsh along the canal
note: The canal "was created in the mid-19th century from local tidal wetlands": the Legislature allowed the creek to be dredged in 1849, dredging "was completed in 1860", deepening allowed 1867; the marsh on both sides was drained and filled with it. Ring = 260 m round today's canal; end year estimated.

name: Bush Terminal: slips between Piers 1-4 filled (Bush Terminal Park)
note: In 1974 the city hired a company "to fill the spaces between Piers 1 through 4"; filling went on through the 1975 fiscal crisis. End year estimated. Ring = Bush Terminal Park + 90 m.

name: Sunset Park waterfront: 2nd Avenue to the bulkhead (Bush Terminal, Army Terminal)
note: Bush Terminal: five piers complete by 1905 between 39th and 51st St; Brooklyn Army Terminal built 15 May 1918 - September 1919. Start year estimated. Inner line 2nd Avenue only brackets the area.

name: Shore Parkway (Belt Parkway) fill, Owl's Head to Bay Parkway
note: The parkway along the Narrows and Gravesend Bay was built on fill (11.8 million cubic yards of hydraulic fill on the whole Belt system) and opened 29 June 1940. Start year estimated. Ring = from 35 m inland of the parkway centre line to the water.

name: Dyker Beach Park: the swamp
note: "In 1918 work began to fill the swampy areas of the park." End year estimated. Ring = the park.

name: Coney Island Creek: the filled middle reach to Sheepshead Bay
note: The creek once ran through to Sheepshead Bay and made Coney Island an island. "By 1924 local land owners had filled a portion"; "a major section was further filled in to allow construction of the Belt Parkway in the 1930s". Ring = a 440 m corridor on the straight line between today's creek head and Sheepshead Bay; the real bed wound. Years estimated inside "1920s and 1930s".

name: Calvert Vaux (Dreier-Offerman) Park fill at the creek mouth
note: "The park was expanded in the 1960s by waste from the construction of the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge"; "more fill was added in 1962". End year estimated.

name: Plumb Beach joined to Brooklyn (Hog Creek filled)
note: "Plumb Beach was originally part of a small island until Hog Creek was filled in during the late 1930s." Years estimated inside that phrase. Ring = Plumb Beach park + 60 m.

name: Floyd Bennett Field: Barren Island joined to Brooklyn
note: Made "by connecting Barren Island and several smaller islands to the rest of Brooklyn by filling the channels between them with sand pumped from the bottom of Jamaica Bay": first contract May 1928 (4.45 million cubic yards over 350 acres), dedicated 26 June 1930, opened 23 May 1931. Later enlargements (1930s, Navy 1941-42) are inside the ring but not dated separately.

name: Marine Park: marsh filled for the park
note: Land given 1920; "development was slow, but with new land purchases, the park grew" by 1937; it is still "mainly a fertile salt marsh". Estimated bracket, no source found with fill dates. Ring = the park.

name: Mill Basin and Bergen Beach: south of Avenue U, Flatbush Avenue to Paerdegat Basin
note: Mill Island and Bergen Island lay in marsh: bulkheads from the late 1890s, Bergen Beach joined to the mainland by 1918 (some say 1911), Mill Island by 1926, the dredge-and-fill "completed by the late 1930s"; more fill at Bergen Beach in the 1980s (not split).

name: Paerdegat Basin, dredged out of Paerdegat Creek
note: A tidal creek until it "came to its present form in the late 1920s" as a straight basin for the Jamaica Bay port scheme. Years estimated inside that phrase. Ring = hull of Paerdegat Basin Park; clip to today's water.

name: Canarsie shore: Seaview Avenue to the bay (Canarsie Park and Pier)
note: Marshy meadow in 1900; "in the early 20th century more than 1 mile of shoreline was filled in with a bulkhead"; park enlarged 1934. Estimated bracket.

name: Starrett City (Spring Creek Towers) peninsula between Fresh Creek and Hendrix Creek
note: Marsh peninsula filled before the housing: site bought for development 1962, complex opened 1974. Estimated bracket, no source found with fill dates.

name: Pennsylvania Avenue Landfill
note: "Filling at the Pennsylvania Avenue Landfill began in 1956"; the city was bound to close and cap both landfills by 1985. Western peninsula of Shirley Chisholm State Park.

name: Fountain Avenue Landfill
note: Began operations "in 1961 or 1963"; closed and capped by 1985. Eastern peninsula of Shirley Chisholm State Park.

name: Spring Creek Park (Brooklyn / Queens line): marsh filled with refuse
note: "By 1948, portions of the park in Brooklyn were landfilled"; temporary landfills ran until the incinerator opened in 1954. Start year is the "by" date.

name: Williamsburg waterfront: Kent Avenue to the bulkhead (Navy Yard to Bushwick Inlet)
note: Shore built out for shipyards, refineries and ferry slips. Estimated bracket; no source found with dates.

name: Greenpoint waterfront: Franklin St / Commercial St to the bulkhead (Bushwick Inlet to Newtown Creek)
note: Shore built out for shipyards and factories. Estimated bracket; no source found with dates.

name: Bushwick Creek and its marsh (McCarren Park to Bushwick Inlet)
note: Filling the creek was proposed in 1896; 42 acres of the former marsh went to McCarren Park in 1905; "the infill operation was completed by 1913". Bushwick Inlet is what remains. Ring = McCarren Park + 250 m and a corridor to the inlet.

name: Ridgewood Reservoir (three basins, Brooklyn / Queens line)
note: Ground broken 11 July 1856, "water was initially raised on November 18, 1858"; third basin 1891; backup only from 1959; "finally decommissioned and drained in 1989" (the middle basin still holds a pond). Ring = hull of the wooded and wet basin floors and the remaining water in Overture (28 ha); the basin walls were not traced.

name: Hunters Point / Long Island City waterfront: Vernon Boulevard to the bulkhead
note: Marsh and shore filled behind the bulkhead. Estimated bracket; no source found with dates.

name: Sunswick Meadows (Queensbridge / Ravenswood lowland)
note: Marshes round Sunswick Creek were drained in the 1870s after outbreaks of disease in 1871 and 1875; "Sunswick Meadows, a lowland north of the present Queensboro Bridge, was infilled with the construction of the bridge in the 1900s and 1910s". Ring = hull of Queensbridge Houses and Park + 220 m.

name: LaGuardia Airport (North Beach): fill into Bowery Bay and Flushing Bay
note: North Beach resort and the small airport of 1929-35 were enlarged to 550 acres: "construction began in 1937", with "landfill from Rikers Island, then a garbage dump, onto a metal reinforcing framework"; dedicated 15 October 1939. Runways were lengthened in 1965-66 (inside the ring, not dated separately). Ring = today's airport; only the part beyond the 1609 shore is made land.

name: Corona ash dump: Flushing Meadow north of the Long Island Expressway, with Willets Point
note: Salt meadow filled with coal ash and street sweepings: "beginning in 1910"; "the filling for the north meadow was complete in 1916"; the Brooklyn Ash Removal Company dumped until its contract ended in 1933 and the city took over 25 May 1934. Regraded 1936-39 for the World's Fair (no new land). Ring = hull of the park north of the expressway and the Citi Field / Willets Point block.

name: Flushing Meadow south of the Long Island Expressway: fill round the new lakes
note: For the 1939 World's Fair "the southern portion of the river was expanded into the Meadow and Willow Lakes" and the marsh round them was filled and graded. Start year estimated (fair works 1936-39). Ring = hull of the park south of the expressway.

name: Meadow Lake (made for the 1939 World's Fair)
note: Artificial freshwater lake made from the upper Flushing River marsh "prior to the 1939 New York World's Fair"; start year estimated. Outline = Overture water.

name: Willow Lake (made for the 1939 World's Fair)
note: Artificial freshwater lake made from the upper Flushing River marsh "prior to the 1939 New York World's Fair"; start year estimated. Outline = Overture water.

name: College Point: Mill Creek and its marsh
note: "Until the mid-20th century, the partially infilled Mill Creek separated College Point from the rest of Queens." Estimated bracket. Ring = hull of College Point Fields and the bus depot + 350 m; it brackets the creek, it is not its outline.

name: Cross Island Parkway fill along Little Neck Bay
note: The west side of the bay had "extensive salt marshes"; the parkway was laid along it (26 % built by February 1939) and opened with the Belt system 29 June 1940. Start year estimated.

name: Alley Pond
note: "By 1954, when the Long Island Expressway was built, Alley Pond was infilled to create the interchange between the two highways." Start year estimated. Ring = 380 m circle on the interchange.

name: Idlewild (John F. Kennedy International Airport): fill on the Jamaica Bay marsh
note: Site on "a large area of marshland on Jamaica Bay" chosen late 1941; "construction began in 1943"; opened 1948. First 1,000 acres, 1,350 more condemned 1944; later enlargements to the present 5,200 acres are inside the ring and not dated separately. Ring = today's airport.

name: Howard Beach east of Cross Bay Boulevard (Old Howard Beach, Hamilton Beach)
note: William Howard "bought more land and filled it in" from 1897 and "dredged and filled the land until he was able to accumulate 500 acres by 1914". Ring = 1 km east of Cross Bay Boulevard, Belt Parkway to 165th Avenue.

name: Howard Beach west of Cross Bay Boulevard (Rockwood Park)
note: "The marshland west of Cross Bay Boulevard was filled in" for post-war houses; Lindenwood to the north "was developed in the 1950s and 1960s on landfill". Estimated bracket.

name: Spring Creek Park, Howard Beach side: refuse fill on the marsh
note: "Landfilling began in Howard Beach on January 17, 1949"; the temporary landfills ran until the incinerator opened in 1954.

name: Broad Channel: fill on Big Egg Marsh
note: The neighbourhood "stands on Big Egg Marsh, an area of fill approximately 20 blocks long and 4 blocks wide"; the Broad Channel Corporation added landfill and laid out streets after leasing the island. Years estimated. Ring = 420 m round the line between Broad Channel American Park and Broad Channel Wetlands.

name: Edgemere Landfill (Rockaway Community Park)
note: "The landfill began operations in June 1938, merging several islands in the Jamaica Bay marshland and connecting them to the main Rockaway Peninsula"; it took waste until 1991.

name: Rockaway peninsula grown westward: Jacob Riis Park to Rockaway Point (natural accretion)
note: Not made land: "the peninsula was gradually expanded westward by the natural accretion of sand from tidal action". Estimated bracket (19th century to the building of the inlet jetty, taken as 1933); the sand spit grew from east to west across the span.

name: Breezy Point Tip (natural accretion behind the Rockaway Inlet jetty)
note: Not made land: sand built up against the jetty at Rockaway Point. Estimated bracket, no source found with dates; jetty year 1933 not verified.

name: Jerome Park Reservoir
note: "Completed in 1906" on the site of the Jerome Park racetrack (closed 1889) for the New Croton Aqueduct. Outline = Overture water.

name: Mott Haven Canal (along Canal Place)
note: A canal dug north from the Harlem River in the mid-19th century (no date found for the digging). "After being declared a nuisance by the Board of Health in 1896 the canal was slowly re-filled, its last segment being in use until 1960s." Ring = 75 m round Canal Place, which keeps its line; the reach south of E 135th St is not covered.

name: Hunts Point: marsh under the markets and the treatment plant
note: Low ground on the Bronx River side of the point under the sewage works and the wholesale markets. Estimated bracket; no source found with dates. Ring = hull of the market and plant sites + 150 m.

name: Port Morris and Oak Point: south of Bruckner Boulevard to the East River
note: Shore flats under the rail yards and piers. Estimated bracket; no source found with dates. The ring also holds natural upland: intersect with the 1609 shore.

name: Bronx shore of the Harlem River: Major Deegan Expressway to the bulkhead
note: Low shore along the river under the rail yards and the expressway. Estimated bracket only; no source found with dates.

name: Soundview Park: landfill over the marsh at the mouth of the Bronx River
note: "Built on landfill over intertidal marshland": dredge-and-fill planned 1938, funding approved March 1939, refuse fill in place by 1942. End year estimated.

name: Ferry Point Park, western part along Westchester Creek
note: Land acquired 1937 for the Bronx-Whitestone Bridge; "the western part of the park along Westchester Creek opened in 1940". Ring = the park west of the bridge; only its marsh edge is made land.

name: Ferry Point Park, eastern part: the cove of Baxter Creek (now the golf links)
note: "The eastern portion was originally a cove that was filled in with landfill by 1970." Start year estimated.

name: Co-op City and Bay Plaza (Freedomland site): fill on the Hutchinson River marsh
note: Marshland of Rattlesnake Creek and the Hutchinson River; "a former municipal landfill" before Freedomland (1960-64); Co-op City (from 1966) "was built on landfill, and the original marshland still surrounds it". Start year estimated.

name: Orchard Beach: LeRoy's Bay and Pelham Bay filled, Hunter Island and Rodman's Neck joined
note: About one third of Pelham Bay was filled "from 1934 to 1938": refuse fill from early 1935 round Rodman's Neck, Twin Island and Hunter Island, sand from 1936, beach opened 1937. The water between Hunter and Twin Islands was filled in 1946-47 (inside the ring, not split). Ring = 520 m round today's beach.

name: Silver Lake Reservoir
note: A natural lake made into a reservoir of the Catskill system; Catskill water first reached it in 1917 (source read through a search summary). Before that the ring held the natural lake. Outline = Overture water.

name: Brookfield Avenue Landfill (Brookfield Park)
note: Municipal landfill run by the Department of Sanitation "from 1966 until 1980" (NYS DEC, read through a search summary). Ring = Brookfield Park.

name: Fresh Kills Landfill
note: Tidal marsh bought 1946 (2,200 acres); the marsh was dredged for the scows and "the landfill accepted its first scow in April 1948"; closed 2001. The mounds grew section by section across the span (not split). Ring = Freshkills Park.

name: Great Kills Park and Crooke's Point
note: "In 1929, the city bought Crooke's Point and adjacent land and started to build a public park"; marsh was raised with 15 million tons of "Sanitation-controlled fill"; opened 1949. Ring = hull of the park.

name: South Beach and Midland Beach: beach and boardwalk fill
note: A 1930 state law paid for "a beach and boardwalk" from Fort Wadsworth to Miller Field; boardwalk built 1935-37. The beach has been widened with sand since; no dated source found for that. Ring = hull of today's two beaches + 60 m.

name: Coney Island: the beach ridge of West Brighton and the West End (shore to Mermaid Avenue)
note: Not fill: barrier-beach sand that the soil survey maps as made land. Dated to the building-up of the resort so that what stood there does not wait decades for its ground (decision 56). Best guess, no dated source; the ring follows data/manual/gapfill/guess_districts.geojson.

name: Rockaway Beach: the barrier beach from Beach 116th to Beach 73rd Street
note: Not fill: barrier-beach sand that the soil survey maps as made land. Dated to the building-up of the resort so that what stood there does not wait decades for its ground (decision 56). Best guess, no dated source; the ring follows data/manual/gapfill/guess_districts.geojson.

name: Arverne and Edgemere: the barrier beach from Beach 73rd to Beach 32nd Street (south of the Edgemere landfill)
note: Not fill: barrier-beach sand that the soil survey maps as made land. Dated to the building-up of the resort so that what stood there does not wait decades for its ground (decision 56). Best guess, no dated source; the ring follows data/manual/gapfill/guess_districts.geojson.
